heroSubtitle: Mitochondrial-derived peptide (16 aa) studied in metabolic-homeostasis and AMPK-pathway research
description: MOTS-c is a 16-amino-acid mitochondrial-derived peptide encoded within the 12S rRNA region of mitochondrial DNA. Published research describes its role in metabolic homeostasis — notably AMPK-pathway signalling, the folate–methionine cycle and muscle insulin-sensitivity models — which is why it is widely used alongside nuclear-encoded peptides in mitochondrial and metabolic research.

faq.question: What is MOTS-c?
faq.answer: MOTS-c is a 16-amino-acid peptide encoded in the mitochondrial 12S rRNA region (CAS 1627580-64-6). Research interest centres on its role in metabolic homeostasis and AMPK-pathway signalling.

faq.question: How does MOTS-c differ from other metabolic peptides in your catalogue?
faq.answer: Unlike GLP-1 receptor agonists such as Semaglutide, MOTS-c is not a GPCR agonist — it is a mitochondrial-derived peptide studied for intracellular metabolic signalling, so the two are used in different research designs.

faq.question: Is MOTS-c sequence and identity documented?
faq.answer: Yes: CAS, molecular formula and molecular weight are stated on the product page and in the downloadable dataset; batch identity is confirmed by mass spectrometry on each COA.
